Heritability on a Line-Mean (Entry-Mean) Basis

Source: R/heritability.R
heritability.Rd

The share of the variance of genotype means that is genetic, from a mixed model with random genotype effects: the standard form for balanced trials and the mixed-model forms of Cullis et al. (2006), Piepho and Möhring (2007) and Oakey et al. (2006) for unbalanced trials, incomplete blocks or correlated errors.

Usage

heritability(
  model,
  genotype,
  method = c("cullis", "piepho", "standard", "oakey", "reliability", "simulated",
    "family", "repeatability", "all"),
  relationship = NULL,
  within_variance = NULL,
  within_n = NULL,
  n_env = NULL,
  n_rep = NULL,
  piepho = c("fixed", "refit"),
  nsim = 10000,
  nboot = 0,
  ncore = 1,
  seed = NULL,
  conf_level = 0.95
)

Arguments

model

An lmer fit, or a gaussian semireg fit, with a random genotype term (1 | genotype). A genotypic variance estimated as 0 gives 0 for every form, with a note.

genotype

Name of the genotype (line, entry, family) factor.

method

"cullis" (default), "piepho", "standard", "oakey", "reliability", "simulated", "family", "repeatability", or "all" (the line-mean forms: standard to simulated).

relationship

For "family": the coefficient of relationship among members of a family.

within_variance, within_n

For "family" and "repeatability" from plot means: the variance among plants within plots and the number of plants per plot (numbers, or names of columns of the data: the mean of the variances, the harmonic mean of the numbers). The single-plant variance is then \(\sigma^2_f + \sum_t \sigma^2_t + (\sigma^2_e - \sigma^2_w/n) + \sigma^2_w\), as Williams et al. (2024, Example 6.2), with \(\sigma^2_e - \sigma^2_w/n\) the plot variance; \(\sigma^2_w\) is taken as known in the standard error.

n_env, n_rep

For "standard", a model with one genotype x environment term: the number of environments and of replicates per environment (n_rep alone: replicates, with the environments from the data); by default both from the data (harmonic means), the only way with several such terms.

piepho

For "piepho": "fixed" (default) or "refit", see Details.

nsim

For "simulated": the number of simulated draws.

nboot

For the mixed-model forms (Cullis to simulated): parametric bootstrap draws for their standard error and percentile limits (each draw refits the model; 0, the default, gives none). The other forms get theirs by the delta method from the covariance of the variance parameters, as varcomp().

ncore

Cores for the bootstrap; results are the same for any number.

seed

Seed for the simulated and bootstrap draws.

conf_level

Confidence level of the limits (logit-normal for the delta method, so they stay in (0, 1)).

Value

A data frame of class "pm_heritability": method, estimate, std.error, conf.low, conf.high; attr(, "components") holds the variance components and the mean variances of differences used.

Details

With \(\sigma^2_g\) the genotypic variance:

"standard"

\(\sigma^2_g / (\sigma^2_g + \sum_t \sigma^2_t / n_t + \sigma^2_e / n)\), over the random terms \(t\) that contain the genotype (genotype x environment, ...), with \(n_t\) the number of their levels per genotype and \(n\) the number of plots per genotype (harmonic means over genotypes; give n_env, n_rep to set them). With one environment and \(r\) replicates, \(\sigma^2_g/(\sigma^2_g + \sigma^2_e/r)\); with \(e\) environments, \(\sigma^2_g/(\sigma^2_g + \sigma^2_{ge}/e + \sigma^2_e/(re))\). Exact for balanced data only.

"cullis"

\(1 - \bar v_{BLUP}/(2\sigma^2_g)\), \(\bar v_{BLUP}\) the mean variance of a difference of two genotype BLUPs (prediction error variance, from the inverse of the mixed model equations, as se_ranef(type = "prediction")).

"piepho"

\(\sigma^2_g / (\sigma^2_g + \bar v_{BLUE}/2)\), \(\bar v_{BLUE}\) the mean variance of a difference of two genotype BLUEs from the same model with genotype as a fixed effect (other random terms kept). By default (piepho = "fixed") its variance components are those of the random-genotype fit, as Schmidt et al. (2019) do, so both terms of the ratio rest on the same estimates (no refit); piepho = "refit" estimates them again, as Piepho and Möhring (2007). On the oats alpha design of John and Williams (1995): 0.808 (Schmidt et al. 2019, Example 2) and 0.803 (Piepho and Möhring 2007, Example 1). (inti::H2cal(emmeans = TRUE) and heritable take emmeans's Kenward-Roger adjusted covariance: 0.797 there.)

"oakey"

the mean of the non-zero eigenvalues of \(I - C_{gg}/\sigma^2_g\), \(C_{gg}\) the prediction error covariance of the genotype BLUPs (the zero ones are directions confounded with fixed effects, as the mean of all genotypes with the intercept). With independent genotypes it equals "cullis" when the intercept is the only fixed effect the genotypes are confounded with; with genotypes nested in a fixed factor (families in provenances) the two differ (a note says so), and with a relationship matrix.

"reliability"

the mean reliability of the genotype BLUPs, \(\bar r^2 = m^{-1}\sum_i (1 - C_{ii}/\sigma^2_g)\) (Schmidt et al. 2019, Eq. 44); it ignores the covariances of the prediction errors, so it is a little below the others for small \(m\).

"simulated"

the expected squared correlation between true genotypic values and their BLUPs, simulated from their joint covariance (Piepho and Möhring 2007; Schmidt et al. 2019, Eq. 41), with nsim draws.

"family"

narrow-sense heritability of a single tree (plant, animal) from families: \((\sigma^2_f/\rho) / (\sigma^2_f + \sum_t \sigma^2_t + \sigma^2_e)\), \(\sigma^2_f\) the family variance (genotype is the family factor), \(\rho\) the relationship among members of a family (1/4 for half-sibs, 1/2 for full-sibs; often taken as 1/3 for open-pollinated progeny, which are partly full-sibs or selfs), and \(\sigma^2_t\) the random terms with the family in them (family x block, i.e. plot; family x site). The other design terms (blocks, rows, columns) are left out of the phenotypic variance. Can exceed 1 when \(\rho\) is too small for the material. Family-mean heritability is the line-mean forms above with the family factor as genotype.

"repeatability"

\(\sigma^2_s / (\sigma^2_s + \sum_t \sigma^2_t + \sigma^2_e)\) with genotype the subject that has repeated records: the share of the variance of a single record due to the subject.

The four line-mean forms agree for balanced data with independent genotypes; with imbalance, incomplete blocks or spatial errors they differ, and Schmidt et al. (2019) recommend the mixed-model forms. Narrow-sense heritability from a pedigree or genomic relationship matrix needs a model with that matrix, which lme4 cannot fit: heritable computes these forms (and the per-genotype \(H^2_\Delta\) of Schmidt et al. 2019) from asreml fits with a relationship matrix. Its standard, Cullis and Oakey values for lmer fits are those of this function (tested); this function adds standard errors, the family and repeatability forms, and advice.

References

Cullis, B. R., Smith, A. B. and Coombes, N. E. (2006). On the design of early generation variety trials with correlated data. Journal of Agricultural, Biological, and Environmental Statistics, 11, 381-393.

Oakey, H., Verbyla, A., Pitchford, W., Cullis, B. and Kuchel, H. (2006). Joint modeling of additive and non-additive genetic line effects in single field trials. Theoretical and Applied Genetics, 113, 809-819.

Piepho, H.-P. and Möhring, J. (2007). Computing heritability and selection response from unbalanced plant breeding trials. Genetics, 177, 1881-1888.

Schmidt, P., Hartung, J., Bennewitz, J. and Piepho, H.-P. (2019). Heritability in plant breeding on a genotype-difference basis. Genetics, 212(4), 991-1008. doi:10.1534/genetics.119.302134

Williams, E. R., Harwood, C. E. and Matheson, A. C. (2024). Experimental Design and Analysis for Tree Improvement (3rd ed.). CSIRO Publishing. doi:10.1071/9781486317110

See also

varcomp, se_ranef

Examples

library(predictmeans)
Oats$nitro <- factor(Oats$nitro)
fm <- lmer(yield ~ nitro + (1 | Block) + (1 | Variety), data = Oats)
heritability(fm, "Variety", method = "all")
#> Heritability on a line-mean basis (95% limits)
#> Variance of Variety 27.45; residual 234.5
#> 
#>       method estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
#>     standard   0.7375    0.2668   0.1587    0.9767
#>       cullis   0.7375        NA       NA        NA
#>       piepho   0.7375        NA       NA        NA
#>        oakey   0.7375        NA       NA        NA
#>  reliability   0.4916        NA       NA        NA
#>    simulated   0.7553        NA       NA        NA
#> 
#> Simulated form: Monte Carlo SE 0.0029 (10000 draws; nsim for more).
# \donttest{
heritability(fm, "Variety", nboot = 199, seed = 1)   # SE of the Cullis form by bootstrap
#> Heritability on a line-mean basis (95% limits)
#> Variance of Variety 27.45; residual 234.5
#> 
#>  method estimate std.error conf.low conf.high
#>  cullis   0.7375    0.3436        0    0.9395
#> 
#> SE and limits of the mixed-model forms from 199 parametric bootstrap draws (percentile).
# }
